Decide on a mock ERP. Half the plumbing is already live and proven: the simulator posts order events to umh-core's erp-receiver and erp-order-bridge writes them into production_orders (136 rows, including both ledger-created orders, written ~2 s after creation). What is missing is something that mints the order id BEFORE approval and sets a production due date — 0 of 136 orders carry one

Price a mock ERP against simply disclosing the inversion — what does closing it actually buy in an integration-partner conversation, and what does a mock ERP cost us in credibility if it is obviously a prop

goals.outcome: Decided: do NOT register umh-actuals-bridge. Registering it would put a second writer on the same trail (it appends every cycle with no hasProgressed check, alongside the poller), and its source view is wrong for per-order evidence anyway: v_oee_by_asset divides runtime by a 24-hour shift window, so a 3m42s order reads 0.4% availability and 0.1% OEE and would fabricate a breach against any OEE floor. Instead the poller now derives the three factors from each machine's own run_time_sec/down_time_sec and cycle_time_ms via GET /api/machines, reporting the line's bottleneck machine. Verified live: 96.6% availability x 73.8% performance x 100% quality = 71.3% OEE. Downtime HOURS are still not recorded — that half of the original motivation stays open under cd8e27d2.
goals.description: Decide whether to register umh-actuals-bridge before contact — today the close-out reports no OEE and no downtime hours, so the record holds less about the run than UMH's own historian does
